headline: Illumina, the DNA-sequencing company, has released SpliceAI2, an AI model that predicts from a DNA sequence alone how genetic changes may disrupt splicing, the cell's cutting and joining of a gene's RNA copy.
score_reason: Lowered from 5: Illumina announced the model on 8 Oct 2026 (per PR Newswire headlines), and the benchmark results are the company's own.
importance_line: Researchers who look for the genetic cause of rare diseases could get a tool that finds more splicing-related variants, including ones deep in non-coding DNA, but the results are Illumina's own and the model was weaker at predicting how a variant's effect changes between tissues.
summary: Illumina, which announced the model on 8 Oct 2026, says in a blog post that its BioInsight AI Lab trained SpliceAI2, the successor to its 2019 SpliceAI tool, on more than 100 times as much data and that it beat its predecessor and two outside models, Pangolin and Google DeepMind's AlphaGenome, on three benchmark datasets, with the AlphaGenome comparison run by collaborators at the University of Oxford. In data from the Genomics England 100,000 Genomes Project it says SpliceAI2 found 17 percent more disease-associated variants than any other splicing model tested, but these are Illumina's own results and the post does not say they have been peer reviewed.
notes: Read in full from the main session's fulltext copy. The source is the developer's own blog post.
